Begin by moving the constant term to the right side of the equation.

 $x^2 - 4x = -3$

We complete the square by taking half of the coefficient of our $x$ term, squaring it, and adding it to both sides of the equation. Since the coefficient of our $x$ term is $-4$, half of it would be $-2$, and squaring it gives us $\blueD{4}$.

 $x^2 - 4x \blueD{ + 4} = -3 \blueD{ + 4}$

We can now rewrite the left side of the equation as a squared term.

 $( x - 2 )^2 = 1$

This is equivalent to

$(x+\blueD{-2})^2=1$
